abstract.t: This document defines AAuth Budgets, an extension to the AAuth Protocol ([I-D.hardt-oauth-aauth-protocol]) that carries a spending ceiling from a person server to a resource. A budget is a ceiling on what an agent may consume at one resource, denominated in a unit the resource declares, carried as a claim in the auth token, and enforced by the resource. Budgets are structurally parallel to scope: the agent asks, the resource offers, the person server and access server may narrow, and the auth token carries what was granted. The extension adds a budget claim to resource tokens and auth tokens, a budget_consumed claim reporting what the presented auth token consumed, a budget_units field and a usage_endpoint to resource metadata, and an AAuth-Budget response header reporting what a request cost and what remains.
